data.narrative:
Electric Hydrogen, a Series C climate and energy technology company, raised $700M to date and carries a current post-money valuation of $1.0B. The valuation is benchmarked against a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA), with primary reference to three same-sector, same-stage peers: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Amogy ($700M, Series C), and Redwood Materials ($6.0B, Series D).

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $1.7B. Peer-median analysis across the three comparables yields a median valuation of $3.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $6.0B. This wider dispersion reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capitalization within the climate energy sector at this stage.

The triangulated analysis produces a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $3.4B (high), with a median of $2.3B. The $1.9B spread between methods reflects meaningful uncertainty around peer selection and applicability. Key sensitivities include capital intensity of commercialization, time to revenue inflection, and technology differentiation relative to the Redwood and KoBold cohort. The current $1.0B valuation sits at the lower bound of this range, suggesting modest upside if execution progresses as planned.
